html:
SMTO-CFG-0008 — The Gateway couldn't start: its connection type for SMTO is invalid

GUID: 457a83ce-69a7-40ab-8ab2-2cc244dfd2ca
Slug: gateway-config-gateway-server-scheme-must-be-http-https
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer, stopped right after starting. The connection type it was given for reaching SMTO, such as https, isn't one it understands. No settings were changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway, find the connection type in the command or settings used to start it: the --server-scheme option (ServerScheme on Windows) or GATEWAY_SERVER_SCHEME. That value is the connection type the Gateway refused.
  2. Change it to https, with no spaces or extra characters. If you aren't sure which type to use, https is the right choice. A Gateway that connects out to SMTO only works over a secure https connection, so other types would fail even if accepted.
  3. If the Gateway connects to SMTO's web address, check that the address starts with https://. If it starts with http://, ask the person who manages SMTO to turn on https. The Gateway can only connect securely if the SMTO server itself offers https.
  4. Start the Gateway again. Then open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection on that Gateway. This shows whether the Gateway now starts with the corrected value and SMTO can reach it.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway keeps running after it starts, and in Settings › Setup › Gateways it shows Connected.

If it still fails

  • Copy the error shown where the Gateway was started (or select Copy error details if SMTO shows it) and send it to the person who set up this Gateway. Mention whether SMTO's web address starts with http:// or https://.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway settings validation rejected server_scheme (GATEWAY_SERVER_SCHEME, or the --server-scheme / -ServerScheme start option) because, after trimming and lowercasing, it is not http, https, ws or wss.

What this means

  • Gateway settings validation rejects server_scheme outside http, https, ws and wss. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway settings validation rejects server_scheme outside http, https, ws and wss.

How to diagnose it

  • Check GATEWAY_SERVER_SCHEME and the intended controller transport/trust configuration.

How to fix it

  • Set GATEWAY_SERVER_SCHEME (or --server-scheme / -ServerScheme) to http, https, ws or wss. Outbound mode only connects over wss, so use https (or wss) and keep the Server's TLS identity trusted by the Gateway, then restart the Gateway.
  • Select the supported scheme matching the actual controller endpoint; preserve its required trust configuration.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Startup accepts the intended supported scheme and normal transport trust checks pass.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
